req.title: Sessions use secret key
req.statement: The system shall sign session cookies with the SECRET_KEY loaded from application config.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-034 requires that session cookies are signed with the SECRET_KEY from application config. Tests must verify: (1) a valid SECRET_KEY produces a signed session cookie that allows authenticated access (positive/EP), (2) a tampered/forged session cookie is rejected (negative/NEG), (3) changing the SECRET_KEY invalidates previously issued session cookies (boundary/STC), and (4) the default 'dev' key is overridden by test config (DT). Each test inspects exact status codes and cookie properties to kill constant-mutation and boolean-negation mutants.

tests.name: test_secret_key_signs_session_cookie_on_login
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a known SECRET_KEY
User 'Rahul' with password 'stone' exists in the database
actions: Inspect the Set-Cookie header for a signed session cookie
expected: Cookie value is a Flask-signed token (starts with dot-separated base64 segments)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_secret_key_signs_session_cookie_on_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'test-secret-xyz'})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    cookie_header = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert 'session=' in cookie_header
    session_val = [p for p in cookie_header.split(';') if p.strip().startswith('session=')][0]
    session_val = session_val.strip()[len('session='):]
    assert len(session_val) > 0
    assert '.' in session_val

test_secret_key_signs_session_cookie_on_login()

tests.name: test_tampered_session_cookie_rejected
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a known SECRET_KEY
A forged/tampered session cookie is crafted manually
actions: Send GET /create with a manually forged session cookie (not signed with the correct key)
Observe that the server does not honour the forged session
expected: HTTP 302 redirect to /auth/login (login_required rejects unauthenticated request)
The forged cookie does not grant authenticated access
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_tampered_session_cookie_rejected():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'real-secret-key'})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    forged_cookie = 'eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoxfQ.ZZZZZZ.ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ'
    client.set_cookie('session', forged_cookie)
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert '/auth/login' in location

test_tampered_session_cookie_rejected()

tests.name: test_changed_secret_key_invalidates_old_session
preconditions: App instance A created with SECRET_KEY='key-alpha'
User logs in and obtains a session cookie from instance A
App instance B created with SECRET_KEY='key-beta' (different key)
actions: Login with instance A to get a valid signed session cookie
Present that cookie to instance B (different SECRET_KEY)
Attempt to access a protected resource on instance B
expected: Instance A login returns HTTP 302 and sets a session cookie
Instance B rejects the old cookie and redirects to /auth/login (HTTP 302)
The session signed by key-alpha is not accepted by key-beta
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_changed_secret_key_invalidates_old_session():
    fd1, path1 = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd1)
    app_a = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path1, 'SECRET_KEY': 'key-alpha'})
    with app_a.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client_a = app_a.test_client(use_cookies=True)
    r = client_a.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    cookie_header = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert 'session=' in cookie_header
    session_val = [p.strip() for p in cookie_header.split(';') if p.strip().startswith('session=')][0]
    session_val = session_val[len('session='):]
    fd2, path2 = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd2)
    app_b = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path2, 'SECRET_KEY': 'key-beta'})
    with app_b.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client_b = app_b.test_client(use_cookies=False)
    client_b.set_cookie('session', session_val)
    r2 = client_b.get('/create')
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    location = r2.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert '/auth/login' in location

test_changed_secret_key_invalidates_old_session()

tests.name: test_secret_key_config_overrides_default_dev_key
preconditions: App created with explicit SECRET_KEY in test_config (not the default 'dev')
actions: Verify it equals the value passed in test_config, not the default 'dev'
expected: The override mechanism works correctly per create_app logic
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_secret_key_config_overrides_default_dev_key():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'my-custom-secret'})
    assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] == 'my-custom-secret'
    assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] != 'dev'

test_secret_key_config_overrides_default_dev_key()

actions: POST /auth/login with valid credentials to obtain a signed session
